summary.text: Julian Bradley is a Republican member of the Wisconsin Senate representing District 28, based in New Berlin, and has been elected to the Senate since 2020.
He chairs the Committee on Utilities, Technology and Tourism and is vice-chair of the Committee on Administrative Rules.

paragraphs.text: Bradley was born in Baltimore, Maryland, on February 11, 1981, and moved to Wisconsin in 1992.
He attended Temple University in 2004-05 and earned a B.S. in political science from the University of Wisconsin-La Crosse in 2014.
The Legislature's page lists him as a full-time legislator and a former realtor and operations manager for Northwestern Mutual and CenturyLink, as well as a professional wrestler.
He is a former chair of the La Crosse County Republican Party and of the 2015 Republican Party of Wisconsin Convention, and a former vice chair of the Third Congressional District Republican Party.
He is also a cofounder of the Together for Tots, Toys for Tots Drive and a member of the Council on Tourism and the Nuclear Power Summit Board.
